functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_paint_color_glyph (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_codepoint_t glyph, hb_font_t *font);
functions.description: Requests painting a color glyph identified by glyph index using funcs’ color-glyph callback. Returns true if painted.
requirements: funcs should have a color-glyph callback installed to have effect.
glyph must be a valid glyph ID for font.
font must be a valid hb_font_t.

functions.name: hb_paint_push_clip_glyph
functions.signature: void hb_paint_push_clip_glyph (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_codepoint_t glyph, hb_font_t *font);
functions.description: Clips subsequent painting to the outline of the specified glyph until a matching hb_paint_pop_clip.
requirements: funcs should have a push-clip-glyph callback installed to have effect.
glyph must be a valid glyph ID for font; outline coordinates are in current font scale and transformed by current transform (per docs).
Calls must be balanced with hb_paint_pop_clip (per push/pop pattern).

functions.name: hb_paint_push_clip_rectangle
functions.signature: void hb_paint_push_clip_rectangle (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, float xmin, float ymin, float xmax, float ymax);
functions.description: Clips subsequent painting to the specified rectangle until a matching hb_paint_pop_clip. Rectangle coordinates are interpreted under the current transform.
requirements: funcs should have a push-clip-rectangle callback installed to have effect.
Calls must be balanced with hb_paint_pop_clip (per push/pop pattern).

functions.name: hb_paint_pop_clip
functions.description: Removes the most recent clip established by a push-clip operation.
requirements: Must be called to balance a prior hb_paint_push_clip_glyph or hb_paint_push_clip_rectangle (per nesting guarantees).

functions.name: hb_paint_color
functions.signature: void hb_paint_color (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_bool_t is_foreground, hb_color_t color);
functions.description: Fills the current clip using either the foreground color or the provided unpremultiplied color, via the installed color callback.
requirements: funcs should have a color callback installed to have effect.
Color passed is unpremultiplied (per docs).

functions.name: hb_paint_image
functions.signature: void hb_paint_image (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_blob_t *image, unsigned int width, unsigned int height, hb_tag_t format, float slant, hb_glyph_extents_t *extents);
functions.description: Renders a glyph image blob using the installed image callback. format identifies the image data (PNG, SVG, or BGRA). Width/height and extents guide sizing/positioning. slant is deprecated and always 0.0.
requirements: funcs should have an image callback installed to have effect.
image must be a valid hb_blob_t with data matching format.
format must be a recognized tag such as HB_PAINT_IMAGE_FORMAT_PNG/SVG/BGRA.
If provided, extents describes glyph extents for desired rendering; may be NULL.
slant should be 0.0 (deprecated per docs).

functions.name: hb_paint_linear_gradient
functions.signature: void hb_paint_linear_gradient (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_color_line_t *color_line, float x0, float y0, float x1, float y1, float x2, float y2);
functions.description: Paints a linear gradient within the current clip using the installed linear-gradient callback. Coordinates are interpreted under the current transform; color_line defines stops and extend mode.
requirements: funcs should have a linear-gradient callback installed to have effect.
color_line is only valid for the duration of the callback (per docs).

functions.name: hb_paint_radial_gradient
functions.signature: void hb_paint_radial_gradient (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_color_line_t *color_line, float x0, float y0, float r0, float x1, float y1, float r1);
functions.description: Paints a radial gradient within the current clip using the installed radial-gradient callback. Coordinates are under the current transform; color_line defines stops and extend mode.
requirements: funcs should have a radial-gradient callback installed to have effect.
color_line is only valid for the duration of the callback (per docs).

functions.name: hb_paint_sweep_gradient
functions.signature: void hb_paint_sweep_gradient (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, hb_color_line_t *color_line, float x0, float y0, float start_angle, float end_angle);
functions.description: Paints a sweep gradient within the current clip using the installed sweep-gradient callback. Center and angles are interpreted under the current transform; color_line defines stops and extend mode.
requirements: funcs should have a sweep-gradient callback installed to have effect.
color_line is only valid for the duration of the callback (per docs).

functions.name: hb_paint_push_group
functions.description: Starts redirecting drawing to an intermediate surface using the installed push-group callback, until hb_paint_pop_group.
requirements: funcs should have a push-group callback installed to have effect.
Calls must be balanced with hb_paint_pop_group (per push/pop pattern).

functions.name: hb_paint_pop_group
functions.description: Stops redirection to the intermediate surface and composites it back using the specified compositing mode via the installed pop-group callback.
requirements: funcs should have a pop-group callback installed to have effect.
Must be paired with a preceding hb_paint_push_group; nesting is guaranteed by the caller.
mode must be a valid hb_paint_composite_mode_t value.

functions.name: hb_paint_custom_palette_color
functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_paint_custom_palette_color (hb_paint_funcs_t *funcs, void *paint_data, unsigned int color_index, hb_color_t *color);
functions.description: Queries a custom palette color via the installed custom-palette-color callback. Returns true and writes color if provided for color_index; otherwise false, meaning use the font palette.
requirements: funcs should have a custom-palette-color callback installed to have effect.
color must be a valid pointer when expecting a true return; may be left untouched on false.
The custom palette is expected to remain unchanged for the duration of an hb_font_paint_glyph() call (per docs).

functions.name: hb_set_create
functions.description: Creates a new, empty hb_set_t instance. Use to hold sets of hb_codepoint_t values (glyph IDs, Unicode code points, etc.). The caller owns the returned object and should destroy it with hb_set_destroy when done.
requirements: Caller must destroy the returned set with hb_set_destroy to avoid leaks.
Function returns NULL on allocation failure; callers should check for NULL before use.

functions.name: hb_set_get_empty
functions.description: Returns an empty hb_set_t instance. Intended for use when a non-NULL, empty set is needed without creating a new one. Details about mutability are not stated in this header; treat usage as read-only unless library documentation states otherwise.
requirements: Returned pointer must be treated as a valid hb_set_t.
Do not assume the returned set can be modified; behavior for mutation is unspecified in this header. If you need a mutable set, create one with hb_set_create.

functions.name: hb_set_reference
functions.description: Increments the reference count of set and returns the same set pointer. Use when sharing a set across components.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
Balance each successful call with a corresponding hb_set_destroy to drop the reference.

functions.name: hb_set_destroy
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of set and destroys it when the count reaches zero.
requirements: set must be a valid hb_set_t pointer or NULL (behavior for NULL is not specified here; avoid passing NULL unless documented elsewhere).
After destruction, the set pointer must not be used.

functions.name: hb_set_set_user_data
functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_set_set_user_data (hb_set_t *set, hb_user_data_key_t *key, void *data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy, hb_bool_t replace);
functions.description: Associates arbitrary user data with set under key. Optionally installs a destroy callback to be called when the data is replaced or the set is destroyed. Returns true on success, false otherwise.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
key must be a valid, non-NULL hb_user_data_key_t pointer that uniquely identifies the data slot.
If data is non-NULL and a destroy callback is provided, the destroy callback must be safe to call at data release time.
If replace is false and there is existing data for key, the function may fail and return false (exact behavior not detailed in this header).

functions.name: hb_set_get_user_data
functions.description: Retrieves user data previously associated with set under key. Returns the stored pointer or NULL if none is set.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
key must be a valid, non-NULL hb_user_data_key_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_allocation_successful
functions.description: Checks whether any memory allocation failures have been recorded on set. Returns false if allocation has failed before; true otherwise.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_copy
functions.description: Creates and returns a new hb_set_t that is a copy of set.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
Returns NULL on allocation failure; callers should check for NULL.

functions.name: hb_set_clear
functions.description: Removes all elements from set, making it empty.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_is_empty
functions.description: Returns whether set contains no elements.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_invert
functions.description: Inverts set membership over the implementation’s domain, toggling the internal inverted flag. Elements previously not in the set become included and vice versa.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
Be aware that inversion changes the interpretation of membership-related operations; use hb_set_is_inverted to query the state.

functions.name: hb_set_is_inverted
functions.description: Reports whether set is currently in the inverted state.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_has
functions.description: Checks whether codepoint is a member of set. Returns true if present, false otherwise.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_add
functions.description: Adds codepoint to set.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_add_range
functions.signature: void hb_set_add_range (hb_set_t *set, hb_codepoint_t first, hb_codepoint_t last);
functions.description: Adds the inclusive range [first, last] to set.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
If first > last the behavior is unspecified in this header; callers should ensure first <= last.

functions.name: hb_set_add_sorted_array
functions.signature: void hb_set_add_sorted_array (hb_set_t *set, const hb_codepoint_t *sorted_codepoints, unsigned int num_codepoints);
functions.description: Adds multiple codepoints to set from a sorted array of codepoints of length num_codepoints.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
If num_codepoints > 0, sorted_codepoints must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to at least num_codepoints elements.
sorted_codepoints must be sorted in non-decreasing (ascending) order.

functions.name: hb_set_del
functions.description: Removes codepoint from set if present.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_del_range
functions.signature: void hb_set_del_range (hb_set_t *set, hb_codepoint_t first, hb_codepoint_t last);
functions.description: Removes the inclusive range [first, last] from set.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
Callers should ensure first <= last; behavior otherwise is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: hb_set_is_equal
functions.description: Compares two sets for equality of membership and returns true if they contain the same elements (respecting inversion state).
requirements: set and other must be valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointers.

functions.name: hb_set_hash
functions.description: Computes and returns a hash value for set, suitable for use in hash tables.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_is_subset
functions.description: Returns true if every element of set is also in larger_set.
requirements: set and larger_set must be valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointers.

functions.name: hb_set_set
functions.description: Replaces the contents of set with a copy of other (including inversion state).
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
other must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_union
functions.description: Modifies set to be the union of set and other.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
other must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_intersect
functions.description: Modifies set to be the intersection of set and other.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
other must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_subtract
functions.description: Removes from set all elements that are also in other (set := set − other).
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
other must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_symmetric_difference
functions.description: Modifies set to contain elements that are in either set or other but not both (exclusive-or of membership).
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
other must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_get_population
functions.description: Returns the number of elements in set (its population).
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.

functions.name: hb_set_get_min
functions.description: Returns the smallest codepoint contained in set. Returns HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID if set is empty.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
Callers should be prepared to handle HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID when the set is empty.

functions.name: hb_set_get_max
functions.description: Returns the largest codepoint contained in set. Returns HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID if set is empty.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
Callers should be prepared to handle HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID when the set is empty.

functions.name: hb_set_next
functions.description: Forward iterator over elements of set. On input, *codepoint must be HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID to start; on success, stores the next element into *codepoint and returns true. Returns false when no further elements exist.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
codepoint must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to hb_codepoint_t.
To begin iteration, initialize *codepoint to HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID.
Between calls, pass back the last value returned in *codepoint to get the subsequent element.

functions.name: hb_set_previous
functions.description: Reverse iterator over elements of set. On input, *codepoint must be HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID to start; on success, stores the previous element into *codepoint and returns true. Returns false when no earlier elements exist.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
codepoint must be a valid, non-NULL pointer to hb_codepoint_t.
To begin iteration, initialize *codepoint to HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID.
Between calls, pass back the last value returned in *codepoint to get the preceding element.

functions.name: hb_set_next_range
functions.description: Iterates forward over contiguous ranges of elements in set. On input, *first and *last must be HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID to start. On success, returns true and sets [*first, *last] to the next inclusive range. Returns false when no further ranges exist.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
first and last must be valid, non-NULL pointers to hb_codepoint_t.
To begin range iteration, initialize both *first and *last to HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID.

functions.name: hb_set_previous_range
functions.description: Iterates backward over contiguous ranges of elements in set. On input, *first and *last must be HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID to start. On success, returns true and sets [*first, *last] to the previous inclusive range. Returns false when no earlier ranges exist.
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
first and last must be valid, non-NULL pointers to hb_codepoint_t.
To begin range iteration, initialize both *first and *last to HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID.

functions.name: hb_set_next_many
functions.signature: unsigned int hb_set_next_many (const hb_set_t *set, hb_codepoint_t codepoint, hb_codepoint_t *out, unsigned int size);
functions.description: Retrieves up to size successive elements after codepoint and writes them into out. Pass HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID for codepoint to start from the first element. Returns the number of elements written (0 when none).
requirements: set must be a valid, non-NULL hb_set_t pointer.
out must point to a writable array with capacity for at least size hb_codepoint_t elements; may be NULL only if size is 0.
Pass HB_SET_VALUE_INVALID as codepoint to start from the beginning.

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_create
functions.signature: hb_shape_plan_t * hb_shape_plan_create(hb_face_t *face, const hb_segment_properties_t *props, const hb_feature_t *user_features, unsigned int num_user_features, const char * const *shaper_list);
functions.description: Creates a shaping plan for a given face and segment properties, optionally constrained by a set of user features and an optional ordered list of shaper backends. Use this to precompute how shaping will be performed for text segments matching the provided properties and features. Details of caching, ownership, and shaper-list termination are not documented in this header; behavior is inferred from HarfBuzz naming patterns.
requirements: face must be a valid hb_face_t pointer (inferred from signature).
props must point to a valid, fully-initialized hb_segment_properties_t describing direction/script/language for the intended text segment (inferred from type usage).
If user_features is not NULL, num_user_features must be the number of elements in user_features; if user_features is NULL, num_user_features should be 0 (inferred from pointer+count convention).
If provided, shaper_list must be a valid array of const char*; termination or allowed contents are unknown in this header (unknown beyond typical HarfBuzz practice).
The returned hb_shape_plan_t* must be released with hb_shape_plan_destroy when no longer needed (inferred from presence of destroy function).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_create_cached
functions.signature: hb_shape_plan_t * hb_shape_plan_create_cached(hb_face_t *face, const hb_segment_properties_t *props, const hb_feature_t *user_features, unsigned int num_user_features, const char * const *shaper_list);
functions.description: Creates (or retrieves) a cached shaping plan matching the given face, segment properties, and user features/shaper list. Intended to reuse existing plans when possible to reduce setup cost. Exact cache semantics are not specified here; name implies internal caching by HarfBuzz.
requirements: face must be a valid hb_face_t pointer (inferred).
props must point to a valid, fully-initialized hb_segment_properties_t (inferred).
If user_features is not NULL, num_user_features must match its element count; if NULL, num_user_features should be 0 (inferred).
If provided, shaper_list must be a valid array of const char*; termination rules are not specified here (unknown beyond typical practice).
The returned plan must be released with hb_shape_plan_destroy when no longer needed, regardless of caching (inferred from API symmetry).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_create2
functions.signature: hb_shape_plan_t * hb_shape_plan_create2(hb_face_t *face, const hb_segment_properties_t *props, const hb_feature_t *user_features, unsigned int num_user_features, const int *coords, unsigned int num_coords, const char * const *shaper_list);
functions.description: Creates a shaping plan like hb_shape_plan_create, additionally parameterized by variation coordinates (e.g., for variable fonts). Coordinates are passed as an array of ints with an accompanying count. Intended when shaping depends on font variation settings.
requirements: face must be a valid hb_face_t pointer (inferred).
props must point to a valid, fully-initialized hb_segment_properties_t (inferred).
If user_features is not NULL, num_user_features must match its element count; if NULL, num_user_features should be 0 (inferred).
If coords is not NULL, num_coords must equal the length of the coords array; if coords is NULL, num_coords should be 0 (inferred).
If provided, shaper_list must be a valid array of const char*; termination rules are not specified here (unknown).
The returned plan must be released with hb_shape_plan_destroy when no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_create_cached2
functions.signature: hb_shape_plan_t * hb_shape_plan_create_cached2(hb_face_t *face, const hb_segment_properties_t *props, const hb_feature_t *user_features, unsigned int num_user_features, const int *coords, unsigned int num_coords, const char * const *shaper_list);
functions.description: Creates (or retrieves) a cached shaping plan like hb_shape_plan_create2, including variation coordinates. Intended to reuse plans across calls when inputs match. Exact cache behavior is unspecified in this header.
requirements: face must be a valid hb_face_t pointer (inferred).
props must point to a valid, fully-initialized hb_segment_properties_t (inferred).
If user_features is not NULL, num_user_features must match its element count; if NULL, num_user_features should be 0 (inferred).
If coords is not NULL, num_coords must equal the length of the coords array; if coords is NULL, num_coords should be 0 (inferred).
If provided, shaper_list must be a valid array of const char*; termination rules are not specified here (unknown).
The returned plan must be released with hb_shape_plan_destroy when no longer needed (inferred).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_get_empty
functions.description: Returns an empty (default) shaping plan object. Typically used as a non-null placeholder. Specific semantics (immutability, singleton behavior, and whether it should be destroyed) are not documented here; in HarfBuzz APIs such objects are usually immutable singletons.
requirements: May return a shared/singleton object; treat as read-only (inferred from HarfBuzz naming pattern).
Do not assume this substitutes for a properly created plan when features, properties, or shaper selection matter (inferred).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_reference
functions.description: Increments the reference count of shape_plan and returns the same plan pointer. Use when sharing the plan across components to manage lifetime via reference counting.
requirements: shape_plan must be a valid hb_shape_plan_t pointer (inferred).
Each successful call should be balanced with a corresponding hb_shape_plan_destroy to avoid leaks (inferred from ref/destroy pattern).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_destroy
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of shape_plan and frees associated resources when the count reaches zero. Safe to call with a valid plan; behavior on NULL is not specified here.
requirements: shape_plan must be either NULL or a valid hb_shape_plan_t previously obtained from this API; passing invalid pointers leads to undefined behavior (inferred).
Every hb_shape_plan_reference or creating function returning a plan should eventually be balanced by a destroy call (inferred).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_set_user_data
functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_shape_plan_set_user_data(hb_shape_plan_t *shape_plan, hb_user_data_key_t *key, void *data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy, hb_bool_t replace);
functions.description: Associates arbitrary user data with the shape_plan under the given key, optionally with a destructor to be called when the data is removed or the plan is destroyed. If replace is false and data already exists for key, the operation may fail. Specific collision and lifetime semantics are not detailed in this header.
requirements: shape_plan must be a valid hb_shape_plan_t pointer (inferred).
key must be a valid hb_user_data_key_t pointer that uniquely identifies the data slot (inferred from HarfBuzz user-data pattern).
If destroy is non-NULL, it must be safe to call with the provided data when the data is replaced or the plan is destroyed (inferred).
replace should be HB_TRUE to overwrite any existing data for the key; if HB_FALSE and data exists, the call may fail and return false (inferred from common pattern).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_get_user_data
functions.description: Retrieves user data previously set on shape_plan for the given key. Returns the stored pointer or NULL if not found. No ownership transfer is implied by this header.
requirements: shape_plan must be a valid hb_shape_plan_t pointer (inferred).
key must be the same hb_user_data_key_t used to set the data (inferred).
The returned pointer remains owned by the shape_plan; do not free it unless you set it and own it (inferred from user-data conventions).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_execute
functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_shape_plan_execute(hb_shape_plan_t *shape_plan, hb_font_t *font, hb_buffer_t *buffer, const hb_feature_t *features, unsigned int num_features);
functions.description: Executes shaping using the provided shaping plan on the given font and buffer, optionally applying an additional list of features. On success, the buffer is transformed to contain shaped glyphs according to the plan. Return value indicates success as hb_bool_t. Detailed error reporting and exact feature handling are not specified here.
requirements: shape_plan must be a valid hb_shape_plan_t pointer (inferred).
font must be a valid hb_font_t associated with a face compatible with the plan (inferred).
buffer must be a valid, initialized hb_buffer_t containing input text and properties matching the plan (inferred).
If features is not NULL, num_features must match its element count; if NULL, num_features should be 0 (inferred).
Caller should check the returned hb_bool_t and handle failure appropriately; no errno or error code is provided here (inferred).

functions.name: hb_shape_plan_get_shaper
functions.description: Returns the name of the shaping backend (shaper) selected for this plan as a null-terminated string. Useful for diagnostics or selecting behavior based on the chosen shaper. Lifetime of the returned string is not documented here; typically it remains valid as long as the plan lives.
requirements: shape_plan must be a valid hb_shape_plan_t pointer (inferred).
Treat the returned string as read-only; do not attempt to modify or free it (inferred).

functions.name: hb_shape
functions.signature: void hb_shape(hb_font_t *font, hb_buffer_t *buffer, const hb_feature_t *features, unsigned int num_features);
functions.description: Shapes the text currently stored in buffer using the specified font and optional OpenType features. Typical usage: create/populate an hb_buffer_t with text and properties, then call hb_shape to produce glyph indices/positions in the buffer for rendering. Returns no status; results are written into the buffer.
requirements: font must be a valid, initialized hb_font_t pointer.
buffer must be a valid, initialized hb_buffer_t pointer that has been populated with input text and appropriate properties (e.g., script/language/direction) before calling.
features may be NULL if no features are to be applied; otherwise it must point to an array of hb_feature_t with length given by num_features.
num_features must be the number of elements in the features array when features is non-NULL; if features is NULL, num_features should be 0 to avoid reading invalid memory.
The function writes shaping results into buffer; callers must read glyph data from buffer after the call.

functions.name: hb_shape_full
functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_shape_full(hb_font_t *font, hb_buffer_t *buffer, const hb_feature_t *features, unsigned int num_features, const char * const *shaper_list);
functions.description: Shapes the text in buffer using the specified font and features, allowing the caller to specify an ordered list of shaper backends to try. Returns an hb_bool_t indicating success. On success, buffer contains glyph indices/positions.
requirements: font must be a valid, initialized hb_font_t pointer.
buffer must be a valid, initialized hb_buffer_t pointer that has been populated with input text and appropriate properties before calling.
features may be NULL if no features are to be applied; otherwise it must point to an array of hb_feature_t with length given by num_features.
num_features must match the number of entries in features when features is non-NULL; if features is NULL, num_features should be 0.
shaper_list must be a valid pointer to a list/array of shaper backend names (exact termination and allowed values are unknown from this header).
Callers must check the hb_bool_t return value; on false, shaping did not succeed and the contents of buffer may be unchanged or undefined.

functions.name: hb_shape_justify
functions.signature: hb_bool_t hb_shape_justify(hb_font_t *font, hb_buffer_t *buffer, const hb_feature_t *features, unsigned int num_features, const char * const *shaper_list, float min_target_advance, float max_target_advance, float *advance, hb_tag_t *var_tag, float *var_value);
functions.description: Experimental API: shapes text with justification constraints, attempting to meet a target advance width range and returning adjustment information. On success, writes shaping results to buffer and updates output parameters: advance (IN/OUT), var_tag (OUT), var_value (OUT). Intended for advanced layout/justification workflows.
requirements: This function is available only when compiled with HB_EXPERIMENTAL_API defined; callers must ensure availability at compile time.
font must be a valid, initialized hb_font_t pointer.
buffer must be a valid, initialized hb_buffer_t pointer that has been populated with input text and appropriate properties before calling.
features may be NULL if no features are to be applied; otherwise it must point to an array of hb_feature_t with length given by num_features.
num_features must match the number of entries in features when features is non-NULL; if features is NULL, num_features should be 0.
shaper_list must be a valid pointer to a list/array of shaper backend names (exact termination and allowed values are unknown from this header).
advance must be a non-NULL pointer to a float and is used as IN/OUT; it will be read and then written by the function.
var_tag must be a non-NULL pointer to hb_tag_t; it will be written by the function.
var_value must be a non-NULL pointer to float; it will be written by the function.
Callers must check the hb_bool_t return value; on false, justification/shaping did not succeed and outputs may be invalid.

functions.name: hb_shape_list_shapers
functions.description: Returns a list of available shaper backend names. Intended for discovery/logging or to build a shaper_list for hb_shape_full-like calls. The returned list is read-only and owned by the library.
requirements: The returned pointer must not be modified or freed by the caller; memory is owned by the library.
The structure/termination of the returned list is not specified in this header (commonly a NULL-terminated array of strings), so callers must consult library documentation to iterate safely.

functions.name: hb_style_get_value
functions.description: Returns a float value representing the specified style metric/axis for the given HarfBuzz font. Style tags include italic, optical size, slant angle/ratio, width, and weight (as defined by the OpenType Design-Variation Axis Tag Registry). Typical usage is to query a font for its recommended style value for a given axis (e.g., current optical size or slant). The precise source of the value (static table vs. variation instance) and the behavior for unsupported tags are not stated in this header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: font must be a valid, initialized hb_font_t obtained from the HarfBuzz API (e.g., created via hb_font_* functions) and must not be NULL.

style_tag must be one of the hb_style_tag_t enumeration values: HB_STYLE_TAG_ITALIC, HB_STYLE_TAG_OPTICAL_SIZE, HB_STYLE_TAG_SLANT_ANGLE, HB_STYLE_TAG_SLANT_RATIO, HB_STYLE_TAG_WIDTH, or HB_STYLE_TAG_WEIGHT.

Interpretation of the return value follows tag-specific conventions documented here: ITALIC is 0 (non-italic) to 1 (fully italic); OPTICAL_SIZE is non-zero and interpreted as text size in points; SLANT_ANGLE is in degrees counter-clockwise and must be > -90 and < +90; SLANT_RATIO expresses slant as a ratio; WIDTH is non-zero and interpreted as percentage of normal width; WEIGHT corresponds to OS/2 usWeightClass / CSS font-weight. These are interpretive constraints for consumers of the value, not additional inputs to this function.
Error handling behavior (e.g., what is returned for unsupported tags or invalid state) is not documented in this header; callers should not assume a specific sentinel value (unknown).

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_get_default
functions.description: Returns the library-provided default hb_unicode_funcs_t, a built-in set of Unicode property callbacks suitable for general use. Typical usage is to pass this to shaping operations when no customization is needed.

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_create
functions.description: Creates a new hb_unicode_funcs_t, optionally using a parent to fall back to for properties not overridden by the caller. Useful for customizing specific Unicode behaviors while inheriting the rest.
requirements: ufuncs parent must be a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t if provided (inferred from pointer usage).
Behavior when parent is NULL is unknown from this header; consult implementation if needed.

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_get_empty
functions.description: Returns an "empty" hb_unicode_funcs_t object. Typically used as a sentinel or base with no behavior; concrete behavior is not described here.
requirements: Specific semantics of the empty instance are unknown in this header.

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_reference
functions.description: Increases the reference count of ufuncs and returns the same pointer. Use to manage shared ownership.
requirements: ufuncs must point to a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t (inferred from typical ref-counted API patterns).

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_destroy
functions.description: Decreases the reference count of ufuncs, destroying it when the count reaches zero.
requirements: ufuncs must point to a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t or follow the library’s NULL-handling contract; whether NULL is allowed is unknown in this header.

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_set_user_data
functions.signature: HB_EXTERN hb_bool_t hb_unicode_funcs_set_user_data (hb_unicode_funcs_t *ufuncs, hb_user_data_key_t *key, void *data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy, hb_bool_t replace);

destroy may be NULL (explicit).
Semantics of replace (when false and key already set) are not described in this header; success/failure conditions are unknown.

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_get_user_data
functions.description: Retrieves user data previously associated with ufuncs via hb_unicode_funcs_set_user_data using the same key. Returns the stored pointer or NULL if none.
requirements: ufuncs must be a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t (inferred).
key must be the same key pointer used during set (inferred from API pattern).

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_make_immutable
functions.description: Marks ufuncs as immutable, preventing further changes to its virtual methods. Useful to finalize a configuration before sharing.
requirements: ufuncs must be a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t (inferred).
Effects on subsequent setter calls are not specified here; typical behavior is that setters are disallowed after immutability (inferred from naming).

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_is_immutable
functions.description: Returns whether ufuncs has been marked immutable.
requirements: ufuncs must be a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t (inferred).

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_get_parent
functions.description: Returns the parent hb_unicode_funcs_t from which this instance inherits behavior, if any.
requirements: ufuncs must be a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t (inferred).

user_data is passed to func as provided (inferred).

functions.signature: HB_EXTERN void hb_unicode_funcs_set_general_category_func (hb_unicode_funcs_t *ufuncs, hb_unicode_general_category_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy);

func must be a valid function pointer implementing hb_unicode_general_category_func_t (inferred).

functions.name: hb_unicode_funcs_set_mirroring_func
functions.signature: HB_EXTERN void hb_unicode_funcs_set_mirroring_func (hb_unicode_funcs_t *ufuncs, hb_unicode_mirroring_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy);

functions.name: hb_aat_layout_get_feature_types
functions.signature: unsigned int hb_aat_layout_get_feature_types(hb_face_t *face, unsigned int start_offset, unsigned int *feature_count, hb_aat_layout_feature_type_t *features);
functions.description: Enumerates AAT feature types present in the font face. Starting at start_offset, it writes up to *feature_count entries (if provided) into features and updates *feature_count to the number written. Typical HarfBuzz list-getter usage allows calling first with features == NULL to learn the required count, then allocating and calling again. Exact return-value convention (total available vs. number written) is not stated here; by convention in HarfBuzz such functions usually return the total number of available items.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized hb_face_t obtained from the font.
start_offset is an index into the feature-type list and should be within [0, total_feature_types]; values beyond the end yield zero items.

feature_count may be NULL; if non-NULL when features is non-NULL, *feature_count must specify the capacity of the features array on input and is updated on output to the number of entries written (conventional HarfBuzz behavior; exact semantics not explicitly documented here).
features may be NULL to query sizes without retrieving data.
Thread-safety and lifetime: face must outlive the call; no ownership of memory is transferred.

functions.name: hb_aat_layout_feature_type_get_name_id
functions.description: Returns the OpenType name table ID (hb_ot_name_id_t) associated with an AAT feature type in the given face. This name ID can be used to query localized strings from the font’s name table for UI display. If the feature type is not present in the font, the returned ID may indicate absence (exact sentinel not stated here).
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized hb_face_t.
feature_type should be a valid hb_aat_layout_feature_type_t; using HB_AAT_LAYOUT_FEATURE_TYPE_INVALID yields unspecified results.
The returned name ID is to be interpreted per the font’s name table; callers should handle the possibility that it does not resolve to a present string.

functions.name: hb_aat_layout_feature_type_get_selector_infos
functions.signature: unsigned int hb_aat_layout_feature_type_get_selector_infos(hb_face_t *face, hb_aat_layout_feature_type_t feature_type, unsigned int start_offset, unsigned int *selector_count, hb_aat_layout_feature_selector_info_t *selectors, unsigned int *default_index);
functions.description: Enumerates selector infos for a given AAT feature type. For the specified feature_type, starting at start_offset, fills up to *selector_count entries of selectors with name IDs and selector enable/disable values. Optionally returns the default selector index for this feature via default_index, or HB_AAT_LAYOUT_NO_SELECTOR_INDEX if none. Typical HarfBuzz two-pass enumeration applies (first call with selectors == NULL to get total count). Exact return-value convention is not explicitly stated; by HarfBuzz convention it usually returns the total number of available selectors for the feature.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized hb_face_t.
feature_type must be a valid AAT feature type supported by the face; otherwise zero selectors may be reported.
start_offset is an index into the selector list and should be within [0, total_selectors]; values beyond the end yield zero items.

selector_count may be NULL; if non-NULL when selectors is non-NULL, *selector_count specifies the capacity of the selectors array on input and is updated on output to the number written (conventional HarfBuzz behavior; exact semantics not explicitly documented here).
selectors may be NULL to query sizes without retrieving data.
default_index may be NULL; if non-NULL, on success is set to the default selector index or HB_AAT_LAYOUT_NO_SELECTOR_INDEX if none.
Callers must not assume the enable/disable selector values are boolean; they are specific selector codes for the feature.

functions.name: hb_aat_layout_has_substitution
functions.description: Returns whether the face contains AAT substitution tables (mort/morx). Use to quickly check if AAT glyph substitution shaping data is present.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized hb_face_t.
Return value is an hb_bool_t indicating presence; no exception is thrown.

functions.name: hb_aat_layout_has_positioning
functions.description: Returns whether the face contains AAT positioning tables (kerx). Use to determine if AAT kerning/positioning data is available.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized hb_face_t.
Return value is an hb_bool_t indicating presence; no exception is thrown.

functions.name: hb_aat_layout_has_tracking
functions.description: Returns whether the face contains AAT tracking tables (trak). Use to check availability of AAT tracking adjustments.
requirements: face must be a valid, initialized hb_face_t.
Return value is an hb_bool_t indicating presence; no exception is thrown.

functions.name: hb_font_funcs_set_glyph_func
functions.signature: void hb_font_funcs_set_glyph_func(hb_font_funcs_t *ffuncs, hb_font_get_glyph_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy)
functions.description: Registers the legacy glyph-mapping callback on a font-functions object. The callback is invoked to map a Unicode code point (and optional variation selector) to a glyph ID. Deprecated in favor of hb_font_funcs_set_nominal_glyph_func and hb_font_funcs_set_variation_glyph_func.
requirements: ffuncs must be a valid, mutable hb_font_funcs_t created by HarfBuzz.
func must be a function pointer matching hb_font_get_glyph_func_t; it will be called with the provided user_data.
destroy may be NULL; if non-NULL it will be called to free user_data when the function is replaced or ffuncs is destroyed.
This API is deprecated; prefer setting nominal and variation glyph callbacks separately.

functions.description: Sets the implementation function used to return the (deprecated) East Asian width classification for a code point. Deprecated as of 2.0.0; HarfBuzz does not use this property.
requirements: ufuncs must be a valid, mutable hb_unicode_funcs_t created by HarfBuzz.
func must be a function pointer matching hb_unicode_eastasian_width_func_t.
destroy may be NULL; if non-NULL it will be called to dispose user_data when replaced or when ufuncs is destroyed.
This API is deprecated and not used by HarfBuzz internals.

functions.name: hb_unicode_eastasian_width
functions.description: Queries the configured East Asian width value for the given code point using the provided Unicode-functions object. Deprecated and not used by HarfBuzz.
requirements: ufuncs must be a valid hb_unicode_funcs_t; if no callback was set, behavior is implementation-defined by the HarfBuzz build.
unicode is a Unicode scalar value (hb_codepoint_t).

functions.signature: void hb_unicode_funcs_set_decompose_compatibility_func(hb_unicode_funcs_t *ufuncs, hb_unicode_decompose_compatibility_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy)

requirements: ufuncs must be a valid, mutable hb_unicode_funcs_t created by HarfBuzz.

The function returns the count of code points written; 0 indicates no compatibility decomposition.

functions.signature: void hb_font_funcs_set_glyph_v_kerning_func(hb_font_funcs_t *ffuncs, hb_font_get_glyph_v_kerning_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy)

functions.signature: void hb_font_funcs_set_glyph_shape_func(hb_font_funcs_t *ffuncs, hb_font_get_glyph_shape_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy)

requirements: ffuncs must be a valid, mutable hb_font_funcs_t created by HarfBuzz.

functions.signature: void hb_font_funcs_set_draw_glyph_func(hb_font_funcs_t *ffuncs, hb_font_draw_glyph_func_t func, void *user_data, hb_destroy_func_t destroy)

functions.signature: void hb_font_get_glyph_shape(hb_font_t *font, hb_codepoint_t glyph, hb_draw_funcs_t *dfuncs, void *draw_data)

functions.name: hb_subset_input_create_or_fail
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new subset input object used to configure what to keep/drop during font subsetting. Returns NULL on allocation or initialization failure. Typical usage: create once, configure sets/flags and axis settings, then pass to hb_subset_or_fail or hb_subset_plan_create_or_fail.
requirements: Caller takes ownership of the returned object and must release it with hb_subset_input_destroy when done.

Returned pointer aliases input; release each acquired reference with hb_subset_input_destroy.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_destroy
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of the subset input and destroys it when the count reaches zero. Frees internal resources and runs any registered user-data destroy callbacks.
requirements: input must be either NULL or a valid hb_subset_input_t previously obtained from this API family.
Do not use the input after its final destroy call.
All user data destroy callbacks associated with the object may be invoked during destruction.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_set_user_data
functions.signature:
hb_bool_t hb_subset_input_set_user_data (hb_subset_input_t  *input,
		       hb_user_data_key_t *key,
		       void *	   data,
		       hb_destroy_func_t   destroy,
		       hb_bool_t	   replace);
functions.description: Associates arbitrary user data with the subset input under the given key. Optionally installs a destroy callback to be called when the data is replaced or when the object is destroyed. If replace is false and a value already exists for key, the function fails.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
key must be a valid pointer used to identify the user data entry; identity is by pointer value.
If replace is false, the call fails if user data for key already exists.
destroy (if non-NULL) must be safe to call when the data is replaced or when input is destroyed.
Returns hb_true on success, hb_false on failure (e.g., allocation failure or replace==false with existing data).

functions.name: hb_subset_input_get_user_data
functions.description: Retrieves user data previously stored on the subset input with hb_subset_input_set_user_data for the specified key. Returns NULL if not present.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
key must be the same key pointer used when setting the data.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_keep_everything
functions.description: Configures the subset input to retain all content (glyphs/codepoints/tables), effectively disabling subsetting drops. Useful as a starting point before selectively dropping items.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
Call before subsetting (i.e., prior to hb_subset_or_fail or creating a plan).

functions.name: hb_subset_input_unicode_set
functions.description: Returns the mutable set of Unicode code points to retain. Modifying the returned hb_set_t updates the input configuration.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
The returned hb_set_t is owned by input; do not destroy it independently (ownership semantics beyond mutation are unspecified in this header).
Modify this set before running subsetting.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_glyph_set
functions.description: Returns the mutable set of glyph indices to retain. Modifying the returned hb_set_t updates the input configuration.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
The returned hb_set_t is owned by input; do not destroy it independently (ownership unspecified here).
Populate this set before subsetting if driving by glyph indices.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_set
functions.description: Generic accessor for one of the configurable input sets (e.g., Unicode set, glyph set, feature/script tag sets). Returns a mutable hb_set_t corresponding to set_type.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
set_type must be one of hb_subset_sets_t enumerators.
The returned hb_set_t is owned by input; do not destroy it independently.
Populate or modify before subsetting.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_old_to_new_glyph_mapping
functions.description: Returns a map that can be populated to override or inspect old-to-new glyph ID mapping for the subset operation. Typically used to pin or remap glyph IDs when RETAIN_GIDS or related flags are involved.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
The returned hb_map_t is owned by input; do not destroy it independently.
Keys and values are glyph indices (hb_codepoint_t range); exact ownership/range semantics are not specified here.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_get_flags
functions.description: Returns the current subsetting flags configured on the input (bitwise OR of hb_subset_flags_t).
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_set_flags
functions.description: Sets the subsetting flags on the input. value should be a bitmask composed of hb_subset_flags_t values.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
value should be a combination (bitwise OR) of hb_subset_flags_t enumerators.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_pin_all_axes_to_default
functions.description: Pins all design-variation axes present in face to their default locations within the input, effectively producing a non-variable subset (for those axes).
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
face must be a valid hb_face_t referencing the source font and should include variation axis data for meaningful effect.
Returns hb_true on success, hb_false on failure (e.g., no applicable axes or internal errors).

functions.name: hb_subset_input_pin_axis_to_default
functions.description: Pins a specific variation axis (identified by axis_tag) to its default position in the input configuration.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
face must be a valid hb_face_t corresponding to the font whose axes are being referenced.
axis_tag must identify an axis present in face; if not found, the function may fail (returns hb_false).

functions.name: hb_subset_input_pin_axis_location
functions.signature:
hb_bool_t hb_subset_input_pin_axis_location (hb_subset_input_t  *input,
			   hb_face_t          *face,
			   hb_tag_t            axis_tag,
			   float               axis_value);
functions.description: Pins a specific variation axis to a given numeric location (axis_value) for subsetting. Useful to freeze a variable font at a particular design location on one axis.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
face must be a valid hb_face_t corresponding to the font.
axis_tag must identify an axis present in face.
axis_value should be within the axis’s supported range for face; out-of-range values may cause failure (returns hb_false).

functions.name: hb_subset_input_get_axis_range
functions.signature:
hb_bool_t hb_subset_input_get_axis_range (hb_subset_input_t  *input,
			hb_tag_t            axis_tag,
			float              *axis_min_value,
			float              *axis_max_value,
			float              *axis_def_value);
functions.description: Gets the current min/max/default values configured for an axis on the input (if any). Returns hb_true on success.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
axis_tag identifies the axis being queried.
Output pointers axis_min_value, axis_max_value, and axis_def_value must be valid (non-NULL) if their values are to be written; pass NULL for any you do not need.
Returns hb_false if no range is set or the axis is unknown to the input.

functions.name: hb_subset_input_set_axis_range
functions.signature:
hb_bool_t hb_subset_input_set_axis_range (hb_subset_input_t  *input,
			hb_face_t          *face,
			hb_tag_t            axis_tag,
			float               axis_min_value,
			float               axis_max_value,
			float               axis_def_value);
functions.description: Configures a min/max/default range for a variation axis on the input. This controls how variable data is retained or reduced during subsetting.
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
face must be a valid hb_face_t corresponding to the source font.
axis_tag must identify an axis present in face.
axis_min_value must be less than or equal to axis_max_value; axis_def_value should lie within [min,max]. (Range sanity is implied by parameter names; exact validation behavior is not specified here).
Returns hb_true on success, hb_false on failure.

functions.name: hb_subset_axis_range_from_string
functions.signature:
hb_bool_t hb_subset_axis_range_from_string (const char *str, int len,
				  float *axis_min_value,
				  float *axis_max_value,
				  float *axis_def_value);
functions.description: Parses a textual axis range specification into numeric min/max/default values. Returns hb_true on successful parse. Commonly used to parse user input like "min:max:def" (exact syntax unspecified here).
requirements: str must point to the text to parse; if len < 0, the string is assumed NUL-terminated (typical HarfBuzz convention, though exact behavior is not stated here).
axis_min_value, axis_max_value, axis_def_value must be valid pointers to receive parsed values (or NULL for fields you do not need).
Returns hb_false if parsing fails.

functions.name: hb_subset_axis_range_to_string
functions.signature:
void hb_subset_axis_range_to_string (hb_subset_input_t *input,
			hb_tag_t axis_tag,
			char *buf,
			unsigned size);
functions.description: Serializes the currently configured axis range for axis_tag on input into a textual form written to buf, up to size bytes (including any terminator).
requirements: input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t.
axis_tag identifies the axis to serialize.
If size > 0, buf must point to a writable memory block of at least size bytes. Contents may be truncated to fit.
The exact output format is unspecified in this header.

functions.name: hb_subset_preprocess
functions.description: Preprocesses the source face to normalize or optimize it for subsetting. Returns a new hb_face_t on success or possibly NULL on failure.
requirements: source must be a valid hb_face_t.
Caller owns the returned face (if not NULL) and must destroy it with hb_face_destroy when done.
The returned face should be used as the input to subsetting functions if preprocessing is desired.

functions.name: hb_subset_or_fail
functions.description: Performs subsetting on source using input and returns a new subset font face. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: source must be a valid hb_face_t to be subset.
input must be a valid, fully configured hb_subset_input_t.
Caller owns the returned face on success and must destroy it with hb_face_destroy.
Check return value for NULL before use.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_execute_or_fail
functions.description: Executes a previously created subsetting plan and returns the resulting subset face, or NULL on failure. Use when subsetting is split into planning and execution phases.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t created by hb_subset_plan_create_or_fail.
Caller owns the returned hb_face_t and must destroy it with hb_face_destroy.
Check for NULL return to detect failure.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_create_or_fail
functions.description: Creates a subsetting plan for face using input. The plan captures mappings and decisions to be used later by hb_subset_plan_execute_or_fail. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: face must be a valid hb_face_t representing the source font.
input must be a valid hb_subset_input_t with desired sets/flags configured.
Caller owns the returned plan and must destroy it with hb_subset_plan_destroy.
Check return for NULL before use.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_destroy
functions.description: Decrements the reference count of the plan and destroys it when it reaches zero, releasing its resources.
requirements: plan must be either NULL or a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
Do not access plan after its final destroy.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_old_to_new_glyph_mapping
functions.description: Returns a map describing how original glyph IDs map to new glyph IDs in the subset according to the plan.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
The returned hb_map_t is owned by plan; do not destroy it independently.
Only valid after plan creation; contents reflect the plan’s decisions.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_new_to_old_glyph_mapping
functions.description: Returns a map describing how new glyph IDs in the subset map back to original glyph IDs.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
The returned hb_map_t is owned by plan; do not destroy it independently.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_unicode_to_old_glyph_mapping
functions.description: Returns a map from Unicode code points to original glyph IDs, as determined by the plan’s closure and mapping logic.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
The returned hb_map_t is owned by plan; do not destroy it independently.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_reference
functions.description: Increments the reference count of the plan and returns the same plan object for shared ownership.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
Release each acquired reference with hb_subset_plan_destroy.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_set_user_data
functions.signature:
hb_bool_t hb_subset_plan_set_user_data (hb_subset_plan_t   *plan,
                              hb_user_data_key_t *key,
                              void               *data,
                              hb_destroy_func_t   destroy,
                              hb_bool_t	  replace);
functions.description: Associates arbitrary user data with the plan under key, with optional destroy callback. Behaves like the corresponding hb_subset_input_* function.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
key must be a stable pointer used as identifier.
If replace is false, the call fails if key already has data.
destroy (if non-NULL) must tolerate being called on replacement or plan destruction.
Returns hb_true on success, hb_false on failure.

functions.name: hb_subset_plan_get_user_data
functions.description: Retrieves user data previously set on plan for the given key. Returns NULL if none.
requirements: plan must be a valid hb_subset_plan_t.
key must be the same key pointer used when setting the data.

functions.name: hb_subset_serialize_or_fail
functions.signature: hb_blob_t *hb_subset_serialize_or_fail(hb_tag_t table_tag, hb_subset_serialize_object_t *hb_objects, unsigned int num_hb_objs);
functions.description: Serializes a provided graph of objects (bytes plus link metadata) into a single binary blob representing a font table identified by table_tag. The object graph is described by an array of hb_subset_serialize_object_t where real_links mark offset fields inside each object that should point to other objects, and virtual_links express ordering constraints (dependents packed after the current object). On success, returns an hb_blob_t* containing the serialized table; on failure, returns null. Typical usage: construct hb_subset_serialize_object_t entries with head/tail set to the object’s byte range and fill link arrays to describe cross-object offsets, then call this function to produce the final table blob. Since: 10.2.0.
requirements: table_tag must be a valid 4-byte tag (hb_tag_t) identifying the table being produced.
If num_hb_objs > 0, hb_objects must point to an array of at least num_hb_objs elements; if num_hb_objs == 0, hb_objects must be either null or a valid (possibly empty) array.
For each hb_subset_serialize_object_t element: head and tail must be initialized pointers defining a contiguous byte range [head, tail); tail must be >= head.
For each object: if num_real_links > 0 then real_links must point to an array of at least num_real_links hb_subset_serialize_link_t entries; if num_real_links == 0, real_links may be null.

For each object: if num_virtual_links > 0 then virtual_links must point to an array of at least num_virtual_links hb_subset_serialize_link_t entries; if num_virtual_links == 0, virtual_links may be null.
For each hb_subset_serialize_link_t in real_links or virtual_links: objidx must be a valid index in [0, num_hb_objs).

For each hb_subset_serialize_link_t in real_links: position (in bytes from the beginning of the owning object’s data) and width (size of the offset field in bytes) must refer to an offset field fully contained within that object’s [head, tail) range; writing the offset must not exceed the object’s size.
The returned hb_blob_t* is heap-allocated by HarfBuzz; the caller owns the reference and must release it with hb_blob_destroy when no longer needed.
The function can fail and return null; callers must check the return value before use.

data_types.description: A short ASCII string representing a four-character OpenType/ISO tag (e.g., 'kern', 'wght'). Input may be longer; only first up to four ASCII characters are significant to form a 32-bit tag.
A lowercase ASCII keyword naming a text direction, typically 'ltr', 'rtl', 'ttb', or 'btt'. Case-insensitive variants may be accepted by the parser.
A 4-letter script code string per ISO 15924 (e.g., 'Latn', 'Grek', 'Arab'). Often case-insensitive; maps to a script enum/tag.
A textual feature specification like 'kern=0', 'liga=1', or 'ss01=2', optionally with range syntax (start:end). Parsed into hb_feature_t.
An OpenType variation axis assignment like 'wght=700', 'wdth=75', or just an axis tag with default value. Parsed into hb_variation_t.
A language identifier string per BCP 47 (e.g., 'en', 'en-US', 'zh-Hant-TW'). Hyphen-separated subtags.
An uninterpreted byte buffer of specified length. May contain any bytes; used to back hb_blob_t memory.
Contents of a given file treated as raw bytes without assumed encoding. Used to create hb_blob_t from a path.
A byte string intended to be valid UTF-8 encoded Unicode text. May include any code points; parser may handle ill-formed sequences by replacement.
Keyword naming a buffer serialization format such as 'TEXT' or 'JSON'. Case-insensitive tag strings are typical.
Glyph buffer serialized in HarfBuzz TEXT format, e.g., space-separated records with fields like gid, cluster, positions as produced by hb-buffer-serialize in TEXT mode.
Glyph buffer serialized in HarfBuzz JSON format; a JSON document containing glyph info/position arrays as produced by serialization in JSON mode.
Unicode input serialized in HarfBuzz TEXT format; textual representation of codepoints/runs as expected by hb_buffer_deserialize_unicode in TEXT mode.
Unicode input serialized in HarfBuzz JSON format; JSON describing codepoints and properties for deserialization.
A short ASCII identifier naming a HarfBuzz face loader backend (e.g., 'ot', 'sfnt', or other implementation-specific names returned by hb_face_list_loaders).
A file whose contents are font data (e.g., OpenType/TrueType, TTC/OTC). Used to create hb_face_t from a file path.
A glyph name such as 'A', 'B.swash', or 'uni0627'. Typically within PostScript glyph naming conventions.
A string specifying a glyph by id or Unicode, commonly 'gidNNN' for numeric glyph id or 'uniXXXX'/'uXXXXXX' for Unicode code point.
A string key selecting a set of hb_font_funcs implementations by name; implementation-specific identifier.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator produces valid ASCII tag strings suitable for HarfBuzz tag-related APIs.
# It focuses on 1–4 character ASCII tags, sometimes NUL-terminated, and sometimes with
# additional trailing data (ignored by hb_tag_from_string when an explicit length is provided).

KNOWN_TAGS = [
    # Common OpenType table tags
    b'cmap', b'head', b'hhea', b'hmtx', b'maxp', b'name', b'OS/2', b'post', b'cvt ', b'fpgm', b'gasp', b'glyf', b'loca', b'prep',
    # Layout/feature/variation/style tags
    b'kern', b'GSUB', b'GPOS', b'GDEF', b'MATH', b'VORG', b'BASE', b'COLR', b'CPAL', b'SVG ', b'avar', b'fvar', b'gvar', b'HVAR', b'VVAR',
    # Script/baseline and miscellaneous
    b'romn', b'hang', b'math', b'Latn', b'Cyrl', b'Arab', b'Grek', b'Hebr',
    # Style axis tags
    b'wght', b'wdth', b'slnt', b'ital', b'opsz', b'Slnt',
]

PRINTABLE_ASCII = [c.encode('ascii') for c in (list(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + string.punctuation + ' '))]


def _rand_ascii_tag(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # 70% choose from known tags, 30% synthesize
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tag = rng.choice(KNOWN_TAGS)
    else:
        # Create 1–4 length ASCII from typical ranges, including space
        length = rng.randint(1, 4)
        tag = b''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII) for _ in range(length))
    return tag


def _maybe_pad_or_truncate(tag: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # hb_tag_from_string may be called with explicit length (1–4), or -1 meaning NUL-terminated
    # Provide variants: exact length, shorter (1..4), or longer buffer with trailing bytes
    mode = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if mode == 0:
        # exact tag
        return tag
    elif mode == 1:
        # ensure length 4 by padding with spaces (common in tags)
        return (tag + b'    ')[:4]
    elif mode == 2:
        # truncate to 1..4
        return tag[:rng.randint(1, min(4, max(1, len(tag))))]
    else:
        # append extra random ASCII bytes that will be ignored if caller passes explicit length
        extra_len = rng.randint(1, 16)
        extra = b''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII) for _ in range(extra_len))
        return tag + extra


def _maybe_nul_terminate(buf: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Sometimes add a NUL terminator (for len == -1 path)
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        # Add exactly one NUL; optionally also add trailing junk after NUL to exercise c_str usage
        if rng.random() < 0.8:
            return buf + b"\x00"
        else:
            # NUL followed by extra bytes (won't be seen by strlen but present in buffer)
            tail = b''.join(rng.choice(PRINTABLE_ASCII) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8)))
            return buf + b"\x00" + tail
    return buf


def _mix_cases_and_spaces(tag: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Randomly vary case and introduce spaces in 4-char tags to hit padding expectations
    out = bytearray()
    for b in tag:
        ch = chr(b)
        if ch.isalpha() and rng.random() < 0.5:
            ch = ch.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower()
        out.append(ord(ch))
    # Optionally replace some bytes with space (0x20) to simulate tags with spaces
    if len(out) < 4 and rng.random() < 0.4:
        while len(out) < 4:
            out.append(0x20)
    return bytes(out)


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose how many candidate strings to concatenate; fuzzer may sample from corpus
    count = rng.randint(1, 5)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(count):
        tag = _rand_ascii_tag(rng)
        tag = _mix_cases_and_spaces(tag, rng)
        buf = _maybe_pad_or_truncate(tag, rng)
        buf = _maybe_nul_terminate(buf, rng)
        parts.append(buf)
        # Occasionally insert newline or whitespace separators to provide multiple c_str opportunities
        if rng.random() < 0.3:
            parts.append(rng.choice([b"\n", b" ", b"\t"]))

    data = b"".join(parts)
    # Ensure size limit
    return data[:4096]

import random
from typing import List

def _pick_direction(rnd: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common canonical names
    canonical = [
        "ltr", "rtl", "ttb", "btt",
    ]
    # Synonyms and variants often accepted by HarfBuzz
    variants = [
        "left-to-right", "right-to-left", "top-to-bottom", "bottom-to-top",
        "hb_direction_ltr", "HB_DIRECTION_RTL",  # enum-like
        "Ltr", "RtL", "TtB", "bTt",            # mixed case
        "LEFTTORIGHT", "RIGHTTOLEFT", "TOPTOBOTTOM", "BOTTOMTOTOP", # shouty
        "east", "west", "north", "south",  # sometimes mapped by implementations
        "+x", "-x", "+y", "-y",            # vector-like shorthands
    ]
    # Deliberately include surrounding whitespace and embedded NUL possibility via len handling
    decorations = [
        ("", ""),
        (" ", ""), ("", " "), (" \t", "\n"), ("\r\n", "\t"),
    ]
    # Choose base token
    pool = canonical + variants
    token = rnd.choice(pool)
    # Randomly change case
    case_mode = rnd.choice(["lower", "upper", "title", "random", "as-is"])
    if case_mode == "lower":
        token = token.lower()
    elif case_mode == "upper":
        token = token.upper()
    elif case_mode == "title":
        token = token.title()
    elif case_mode == "random":
        token = "".join(ch.upper() if rnd.random() < 0.5 else ch.lower() for ch in token)
    # Add some optional punctuation or separators to explore len semantics
    if rnd.random() < 0.25:
        token += rnd.choice(["\0ignored", " extra", "\ttrail", ",more", "/rest"])
    pre, post = rnd.choice(decorations)
    s = pre + token + post
    # Keep within 4096 bytes
    return s[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rnd = random.Random(seed)
    # With some probability return a valid canonical token to seed corpus with strong signals
    if rnd.random() < 0.6:
        s = _pick_direction(rnd)
    else:
        # Also include obviously invalid or empty to allow parser to hit invalid branch
        choices: List[str] = ["", "invalid", "none", "middle", "horizontal", "vertical"]
        s = rnd.choice(choices)
        # Randomly tweak case and add whitespace
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            s = s.upper()
        if rnd.random() < 0.5:
            s = " " + s + " "
    return s.encode("utf-8", errors="strict")

# The fuzzer stub calls FUZZ_PARAM_STR() once. Our generator returns a bytes buffer

# We therefore produce a byte sequence containing one interesting script string.
# Keep under 4096 bytes and deterministic per seed.

# A curated list of valid ISO 15924 script codes commonly used by HarfBuzz.
# Includes a spread of cases (proper case, upper, lower) and some edge-cases like empty and short.
_SCRIPT_CODES: List[str] = [
    # Very common
    "Latn", "latn", "LATN",
    "Grek", "Arab", "Hebr", "Cyrl", "Hans", "Hant", "Hani", "Hang",
    # South Asian
    "Deva", "Beng", "Gujr", "Guru", "Knda", "Mlym", "Orya", "Taml", "Telu", "Sinh",
    # SE/E Asia
    "Thai", "Laoo", "Mymr", "Khmr", "Java", "Bali", "Tibt",
    # Others
    "Ethi", "Armn", "Geor", "Runr", "Ogam", "Cprt", "Phnx", "Khmr", "Mong",
    # Newer/less common
    "Cans", "Cher", "Tfng", "Vaii", "Olck", "Sund", "Lisu", "Yiii",
    # Symbols / special groupings sometimes relevant
    "Zyyy",  # Common
    "Zinh",  # Inherited
    "Zmth",  # Math
    "Zsym",  # Symbols (not an hb enum but ISO 15924 valid tag)
    "Xsux",  # Cuneiform
    # Vertical variants sometimes used with fonts
    "Kana", "Hira",
]

# Some intentionally short/long and boundary cases: hb_script_from_string takes length explicitly,
# so shorter lengths will be tested by the stub; we only need to provide the underlying string.
_EXTRA_CASES: List[str] = [
    "",          # empty
    "A",         # 1-char
    "Ab",        # 2-char
    "Abc",       # 3-char
    "LatnExtra", # longer than 4
    "grek",      # lowercase variant
    "ARAB",      # uppercase variant
    "Hebr\0junk",# embedded NUL (after 4 chars) to check handling if consumer reads C-string
]

# Include a broad selection including tags present in the provided hb_script_t enum list

_ODD_STRINGS: List[str] = [
    "1234", "!!!!", "Ab1$", "    ", "\t\n\r ", "Lat ", " L atn ",
]


def _random_case_variant(rng: random.Random, s: str) -> str:
    # Randomly vary case per character
    chars = [c.upper() if rng.random() < 0.5 else c.lower() for c in s]
    return "".join(chars)


def _make_candidate(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    choice_pool = []
    # Bias toward known-good 4-letter tags
    choice_pool.extend(_SCRIPT_CODES * 4)
    choice_pool.extend(_ENUM_SCRIPTS * 2)
    choice_pool.extend(_EXTRA_CASES)
    choice_pool.extend(_ODD_STRINGS)

    base = rng.choice(choice_pool)

    # Occasionally synthesize a random 4-letter alpha tag
    if rng.random() < 0.25:
        base = "".join(rng.choice("ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz") for _ in range(4))

    # Random chance to change casing
    if rng.random() < 0.5 and len(base) >= 1:
        base = _random_case_variant(rng, base)

    # Occasionally append or prepend whitespace or punctuation to test explicit length handling
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        pad_left = rng.choice(["", " ", "\t"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
        pad_right = rng.choice(["", " ", "\n"]) if rng.random() < 0.7 else ""
        base = pad_left + base + pad_right

    # Ensure total size stays small
    return base[:32]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Create one or more candidate strings concatenated with separators to allow FUZZ_PARAM_STR
    # infrastructure to pick a contiguous slice; but typically only the first string is used.
    # We provide a single candidate to keep it focused and valid.
    s = _make_candidate(rng)

    # Return as UTF-8 bytes, no trailing NUL (the harness provides length explicitly and C-string view).
    data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')

    # Safety: cap size
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data

import random

# Generator for HarfBuzz hb_variation_from_string inputs
# Expects strings like:
#   wght=700
#   wdth=75
#   ital=1
#   slnt=-10
#   opsz=12.0
# Also allows just the tag (defaults value), and supports whitespace and list forms.

AXES = [
    # Common registered axes
    "wght", "wdth", "opsz", "ital", "slnt",
    # Additional plausible/custom axes
    "GRAD", "XOPQ", "YOPQ", "XTRA", "YTRA", "CNTR",
    "SWSH", "SOFT", "HCON", "VCON", "SPAC", "ROND",
    # Lowercase variants
    "grad", "xopq", "yopq", "xtra", "ytra", "cntr",
]

WHITESPACE = ["", " ", "\t", "\n", "\r\n"]
SEPARATORS = [",", ";", "/", " "]


def _rand_float(rng: random.Random) -> float:
    # Generate a float across useful ranges including negatives and decimals
    modes = [
        lambda: rng.uniform(-1000.0, 1000.0),
        lambda: rng.uniform(-1.0, 1.0),
        lambda: float(rng.randrange(-1000, 1001)),
        lambda: rng.choice([0.0, 1.0, -1.0, 100.0, 400.0, 700.0, 900.0, 12.0, 14.0, 16.0]),
    ]
    v = rng.choice(modes)()
    # Round sometimes to integer-ish or one decimal
    roll = rng.random()
    if roll < 0.3:
        v = round(v)
    elif roll < 0.6:
        v = round(v, 1)
    return v


def _fmt_value(v: float, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Format as integer, float, or with exponent occasionally
    fmt_choice = rng.random()
    if fmt_choice < 0.55:
        # integer if close
        if abs(v - round(v)) < 1e-6:
            return str(int(round(v)))
        return ("%g" % v)
    elif fmt_choice < 0.9:
        return ("%.3f" % v).rstrip("0").rstrip(".")
    else:
        # scientific
        return ("%e" % v)


def _maybe_space(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    return rng.choice(WHITESPACE)


def _random_axis(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # 4-byte tags; sometimes random letters
    if rng.random() < 0.75:
        return rng.choice(AXES)
    # generate random alpha 4 chars (case preserved)
    tag = ''.join(rng.choice([chr(rng.randrange(ord('A'), ord('Z')+1)), chr(rng.randrange(ord('a'), ord('z')+1))]) for _ in range(4))
    return tag


def _make_assignment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    axis = _random_axis(rng)
    # Sometimes just the tag without value
    if rng.random() < 0.15:
        return f"{axis}"
    # Sometimes use colon instead of equals; HarfBuzz accepts '=' and likely ':'
    # but to stay conservative, prefer '='; small chance ':'
    eq = '=' if rng.random() < 0.9 else ':'
    v = _fmt_value(_rand_float(rng), rng)
    return f"{axis}{_maybe_space(rng)}{eq}{_maybe_space(rng)}{v}"


def _wrap_noise(s: str, rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Add optional surrounding whitespace
    pre = _maybe_space(rng)
    post = _maybe_space(rng)
    # Optionally add parentheses
    if rng.random() < 0.1:
        s = f"({s})"
    return pre + s + post


def _build_list(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build a list of assignments separated by commas/semicolons/spaces
    n = rng.randrange(1, 5)  # 1..4 items
    parts = []
    for i in range(n):
        parts.append(_make_assignment(rng))
    sep = rng.choice(SEPARATORS)
    # Allow optional spaces around separators
    if sep.strip() != "":
        sep = _maybe_space(rng) + sep + _maybe_space(rng)
    s = sep.join(parts)
    # Sometimes include mixed separators
    if rng.random() < 0.2 and n > 2:
        alt = rng.choice(SEPARATORS)
        if alt.strip() != "":
            alt = _maybe_space(rng) + alt + _maybe_space(rng)
        idx = rng.randrange(1, n-1)
        tokens = parts[:]
        s = sep.join(tokens[:idx]) + alt + sep.join(tokens[idx:])
    return _wrap_noise(s, rng)


def _truncate_randomly(data: bytes, rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # hb_variation_from_string takes a pointer and explicit length; the fuzzer
    # may pass a random len up to size, so providing data that remains valid when
    # truncated early can expose additional paths. We therefore ensure early
    # substrings are self-contained assignments too by optionally prefixing with
    # a single assignment followed by separator and more content.
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        a = _make_assignment(rng)
        b = _build_list(rng)
        sep = rng.choice([",", ";", " "]) + _maybe_space(rng)
        combined = (a + sep + b).encode('utf-8')
        return combined[:4096]
    return data[:4096]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # Choose among: single assignment, list, or tag-only
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.35:
        s = _wrap_noise(_make_assignment(rng), rng)
    elif choice < 0.8:
        s = _build_list(rng)
    else:
        # tag only
        s = _wrap_noise(_random_axis(rng), rng)
    data = s.encode('utf-8')
    return _truncate_randomly(data, rng)
